english.title: Begging in a public place - second or subsequent occasion
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) placed yourself in a public place, street, highway, court or passage namely **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..) to beg or gather alms
english.legislation: Contrary to section 3 of the Vagrancy Act 1824 and section 70 of the Criminal Justice Act 1982.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
placed yourself in a public place/street/highway/court/passage to beg/gather alms
second /subsequent occasion

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Mandatory drug test required if 18 or over
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence should not be used after 28th June 2026 due to repeal by the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022.
(ii) Made a recordable offence as from 1/12/03 by the National Police Records (Recordable Offences)(Amendment) Regulations 2003.

other.powersofarrest: Any person' includes a constable. section 26 of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 did not abolish this power (confirmed in Gapper v C.C. of Avon and Somerset 1998).
other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level three on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months
